READ-ONLY exploration in /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. Do not edit anything. You may use `gh` CLI and git commands to read PRs.

CONTEXT: Two merged PRs are treated as the canonical exemplars that establish "how we build UI" on this project. I need the concrete, checkable patterns they establish, so a workflow skill can enforce them.

- PR #59 — https://github.com/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/pull/59 (feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui, merged as 8362b3c)
- PR #56 — https://github.com/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/pull/56 (the design-token foundation cleanup)

Search breadth: very thorough.

Report on:

1. **PR #56 — the token layer.** What did it change in `overrides/app/theme/foundation/`? It reportedly cut hand-typed literals from 237 to 64 by removing 173 duplicates. What is the resulting token architecture — what files define tokens, what naming scheme (`var(--zimm-*)`), how do tokens get emitted, and what is the rule for when a raw literal is acceptable? Read `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` to understand what it enforces and what the `audit-allow:` / `provisional` escape hatch is.

2. **PR #59 — the component + CSS layer.** This built the global footer. Report the file structure it established: how a component directory is laid out (index.tsx, *.css.ts, *.stories.tsx, *.test.tsx?), how a "focused" recipe (e.g. `footer/footerNavColumn/footerNavColumn.css.ts`) differs from a "shared" style surface (`theme/components/footerShared.ts`), and what the decision rule appears to be for putting a style in one versus the other.

3. **The atoms/molecules/organisms taxonomy as actually practised.** Look at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/`. What genuinely distinguishes an atom from a molecule from an organism here? Give the clearest 2-3 examples of each and what makes them that tier. Is the taxonomy documented anywhere or only implied by placement?

4. **The override vs. custom decision.** How do you tell when work should override a Salesforce retail-react-app base file versus create a new custom component under ui-kits? Cite any documented rule and any evidence from these two PRs.

5. **Contentful integration in builds.** How does a component become Contentful-aware? Look at `overrides/app/components/contentful/` and any registration path. What are the content types involved and what does a developer have to do to wire a component up?

For each pattern, give me file paths and, where a rule is stated in code or docs, cite file:line. Prefer concrete examples over generalities. Return a structured report.

Builds the global footer per SFCC-55 — shell, layout, and component structure across
all eight storefronts and both breakpoints. Content is Contentful-shaped but
fixture-backed: the CMS integration, link destinations, and Omneo sign-up are
separate stories, so `FooterContainer` supplies `FOOTER_FIXTURE` and `Footer` itself
takes its content as a required prop and fetches nothing.

Six ui-kit atoms/molecules were built or completed alongside it — logo, icon,
nav-item, button, text-input, and the input-action molecule — all six consumed by
the footer.

Three points worth surfacing before review:

- **Fonts are now self-hosted**, reversing the position stated in #53. Futura Round
  renders in-app and in Storybook from one shared `@font-face` module. The fallback
  stack measures ~13% wider, so several sizing decisions made against it were wrong
  and were redone once real metrics were in play. Licence files are deliberately
  excluded from the repository.
- **This branch was taken over from Jersey.** Their three CodeRabbit-fix commits are
  in the history; the parts worth keeping were adopted deliberately as separate
  commits (`fix(button)`, `feat(footer)`, `test(ui-kit)`) rather than folded into
  conflict resolution, so what came from upstream and why stays visible.
- **9 of the 16 new commits carry `.claude/registry/` churn.** The `pre-commit` hook
  regenerates it on any `components/`/`hooks/`/`utils/` change and `git add`s it.
  Mechanical — skip those hunks.

`header/index.tsx` carries a pre-existing `fontSize="l"` (invalid token) and a
`useCurrentBasket` call from the original copy-first import. Both predate this PR —
our diff there is comments only — but they surface in the changed-files view.

- Ticket: **SFCC-55** (Global Footer UI). Design: Figma *Zimmermann_Design_System_2026*;
  footer frames signed off with Dani & Vicky (2026-07-07). Test cases SFCC-T116 – SFCC-T122

- `components/footer/` — footer assembly, subscribe section + modal, contact icon row,

2	name: new-component
3	description: Scaffold a new Zimmermann component under overrides/app/components/ — TypeScript, Chakra-first, with a paired Storybook story. Use whenever a new custom component is needed.
4	---
5	
6	Scaffold a new Zimmermann custom component.
7	
8	The component name is: $ARGUMENTS
9	
10	## Conventions
11	
12	Follow [.claude/rules/conventions.md](../../rules/conventions.md) (naming, folder layout,
13	cross-cutting rules), [components.md](../../rules/components.md) (props types, JSDoc policy,
14	composition, Storybook categorisation), and [css.md](../../rules/css.md) (Chakra token usage)
15	— together the single source of truth for scaffolding. Higher-level project rules live in
16	[AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md). Do not restate rules here — read those files before
17	scaffolding.
18	
19	Key implications for scaffolding:
20	- Component lives in its own folder: `componentName/index.tsx` (Zimmermann-authored) or
21	  `component-name/index.tsx` (override of a base SF component).
22	- Props type named `<ComponentName>Props`, declared at the top of `index.tsx` by default.
23	- Storybook story is mandatory; Vitest only when the component owns non-trivial logic.
24	
25	## Steps
26	
27	1. Read one nearby existing custom component under [overrides/app/components/](../../../overrides/app/components/) to match code style, import order, and Chakra usage. If no Zimmermann-authored component exists yet, read a base template component from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/` and convert the style to TypeScript + Chakra props.
28	
29	2. Create `overrides/app/components/<componentName>/index.tsx`:
30	   - Functional React component, named export (`export function <ComponentName>`) plus default export.
31	   - `type <ComponentName>Props = { ... }` at the top of the file.
32	   - JSDoc above the component if it will be consumed by ≥2 callers (shared/Tier 2).
33	   - Chakra primitives for layout (`Box`, `Flex`, `Text`, etc.) using theme tokens — no hardcoded hex, pixel spacing, or raw font sizes.
34	   - No data-fetching hooks of any kind (commerce SDK hooks like `useCurrentBasket`/`useCurrentCustomer`/`useProduct`, or React Query) — accept data as props; the parent (a page or container component) owns data fetching. See components.md → Composition → Container/presentational separation. Exception: Context-backed, app-wide static-content hooks (`useIntl`, `useUiCopy`) may be called directly — they read from a Provider mounted once at the app root and degrade gracefully with none present, so they don't create the reuse problem this rule exists to prevent. See components.md's exception note for the full reasoning.
35	
36	3. Create `overrides/app/components/<componentName>/index.stories.tsx` — but first decide
37	   if a story is needed at all. Per [components.md](../../rules/components.md) →
38	   **Storybook**, purely internal sub-components that only render inside one parent
39	   don't need their own story; cover their variants via the parent. If a story *is* needed:
40	   - Storybook 8.6 CSF3 default export.
41	   - Pick the right category prefix from components.md — `Foundation/`, `Elements/`,
42	     `Layout/`, `Commerce/`, `Forms/`, `Pages/`, or `Contentful/`. Ask the developer if it's
43	     not obvious which one fits (with your recommendation).
44	   - `title: '<Category>/<ComponentName>'` (e.g. `'Commerce/ProductTile'`,
45	     `'Layout/Header'`).
46	   - At least one named export `Default`. Add named exports for meaningful states only —
47	     not every prop combination.
48	   - Add a `play` function only if the component has interactive behaviour worth asserting.
49	
50	4. If the component owns non-trivial logic (branching, prop→JSX mapping decisions, event wiring), create `index.test.ts`/`index.test.tsx` (Vitest) in the same folder — even if that logic's effects are also covered by a hook's own test or a parent's assembly-level Storybook `play`. Resolve any duplication by mocking the hook/child whose internals are proven elsewhere and testing only this component's own contract, not by skipping the file. See testing.md's note under "What to test (and what to skip)". Skip only when the component has no branching/decision logic at all (pure prop interpolation).
51	
52	5. Optional: if the props type exceeds ~30 lines or will be consumed by sibling files, move it to `types.ts` in the same folder. Otherwise leave it inline.
53	
54	6. Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and confirm zero new errors.
55	
56	## Constraints
57	
58	- Do not modify any existing files (no auto-wiring into routes, parents, or the theme registry).
59	- Do not add npm packages — see [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) Hard Rule 7.
60	- Do not import from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` source directly — re-export from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` paths.
61	- For new icons, use `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons`; if a needed icon is missing, ask the developer.
62	
63	## Output
64	
65	Tell the developer:
66	- The paths of every file created.
67	- The import to copy: `import <ComponentName> from '.../components/<componentName>'` (no filename — resolves via `index.tsx`).
68	- A one-sentence note on where it likely wires in, or ask if unsure.
69	- A reminder that `npx tsc --noEmit` was run and passed.

1	---
2	name: contentful-register-component
3	description: Register a Zimmermann React component with Contentful Studio Experiences. Use when a developer asks to register, add, or expose a React component to Contentful, or when they need to create a Contentful component definition for an existing component.
4	allowed-tools: Read, Edit, Bash
5	---
6	
7	# Contentful Component Registration
8	
9	Studio Experiences definitions are now **generated from code** — you never write a
10	`defineComponents` entry by hand. The source of truth is the component's `Props` type,
11	annotated with `@cf` JSDoc tags.
12	
13	## Steps
14	
15	### 1. Move the component into `experiences/`
16	
17	The codegen only processes files under
18	`overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/`. If the component isn't there yet,
19	move it (or create it) in that folder.
20	
21	### 2. Add `/** @cf-register */` to the component
22	
23	Place it immediately before the component's `const` declaration:
24	
25	```tsx
26	/** @cf-register */
27	const MyComponent = ({ ... }: MyComponentProps) => { ... };
28	
29	export default MyComponent;
30	```
31	
32	### 3. Annotate every prop in the `Props` type
33	
34	Props without a `@cf` tag are silently skipped — omitting the tag is how you exclude a prop from the Contentful definition.
35	
36	```tsx
37	type MyComponentProps = {
38	  /** @cf Headline */
39	  headline: string;
40	
41	  /** @cf Body Copy, longText */
42	  body?: string;
43	
44	  /** @cf Hero Image, media */
45	  heroImage?: string;
46	
47	  /** @cf Layout, select */
48	  layout?: 'left' | 'right';
49	
50	  internalId?: string;
51	};
52	```
53	
54	**Tag syntax:**
55	
56	| Tag | Meaning |
57	|-----|---------|
58	| `/** @cf Display Name */` | Infer control from the TS type (see table below) |
59	| `/** @cf Display Name, control */` | Override the inferred control |
60	
61	Props without any `@cf` tag are silently skipped — no tag needed to exclude a prop.
62	
63	**Type → control inference table:**
64	
65	| TypeScript type | Inferred control | Contentful variable type |
66	|----------------|-----------------|--------------------------|
67	| `string` | `shortText` | Text |
68	| `boolean` | `toggle` | Boolean |
69	| `number` | `number` | Number |
70	| string literal union (`'a' \| 'b'`) | `select` | Text |
71	
72	**Valid explicit controls:** `shortText`, `longText`, `select`, `toggle`, `number`, `media`
73	
74	**Auto-skipped:** props starting with `on` (event handlers), `children` (emits
75	`children: true` on the component registration instead), and any prop with no `@cf` tag.
76	
77	### 4. Run the generator
78	
79	```bash
80	npm run generate:contentful
81	```
82	
83	This rewrites `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts`
84	automatically. Verify the output looks correct, then commit both the annotated
85	component and the updated `definitions.ts`.
86	
87	### 5. Verify
88	
89	```bash
90	npx tsc --noEmit
91	npm run generate:contentful:check
92	```
93	
94	`--check` exits zero if `definitions.ts` is in sync with the source files.
95	
96	---
97	
98	## Notes
99	
100	- **Never edit `definitions.ts` by hand** — it is autogenerated and will be overwritten
101	  on the next run.
102	- The pre-commit hook auto-runs the generator whenever an `experiences/*.tsx` file is
103	  staged, so `definitions.ts` stays in sync automatically.
104	- `children: ReactNode` → use `children: true` convention; the generator handles this
105	  automatically when it sees a `children` prop.
106	- `thumbnailUrl` is left blank until a real Contentful account exists.
107	- Component `id` is auto-derived as kebab-case of the filename
108	  (`myComponent.tsx` → `my-component`).
109	- Component `name` is auto-derived as Title Case of the id words
110	  (`my-component` → `My Component`).

## Overrides Pattern

All customizations live in `overrides/` mirroring the structure of `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/`. Never edit `node_modules/`.

**Minimise custom code.** When implementing Zimmermann's design and layout, stay as close to the base PWA Kit implementation as possible. Style changes (CSS, Chakra props, theme tokens) are always expected and need no confirmation. Structural changes — restructuring components, altering data flow, or significantly deviating from base template behaviour — must be confirmed with the user before proceeding.

**Before any change:** check whether the file exists in `overrides/`. If not, create the override:

1. Copy from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path in `overrides/`.
2. Rename `.js`/`.jsx` → `.ts`/`.tsx`. Replace `PropTypes` with TypeScript `type` definitions. Add explicit types to all parameters, return values, and props. Use Commerce SDK types (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`, `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`) where available. No `as any` or `// @ts-ignore`.
3. Verify `npx tsc --noEmit` passes with zero errors.
4. **Stop. Present the converted file to the user and wait for approval before making any functional changes.**

## New vs. Override Components

- **Overriding a base template component:** copy from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path in `overrides/` (see Overrides Pattern above).
- **Brand-new components** (no base template equivalent): create them in `overrides/app/components/custom/`.

## Key Paths

- **Country/locale/currency mappings:** `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` — single source of truth for URL slugs, locales, currencies, shipping countries, Global-e flag, and boutique regions. When adding a market also update `config/sites.js`.
- **Contentful config:** `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts` — always render locale-specific content using Contentful's native localisation fields. Gate preview/draft content behind a server-side check; never expose draft content in production.
- **Theme / design tokens:** `overrides/app/theme/` — `index.ts` composes the theme; brand tokens live in `foundation/` (colour, fonts, typography, gridSystem, spacing, sizes, motion, and the `--zimm-*` registry in `zimmTokens.ts` — Tier 1, UI Designer owned); the `.zimm-*` global classes composed from them live in `globalStyles.ts` (Tier 2); a per-component override lives either one file each in `components/` (e.g. `header.ts`, `listMenu.ts` — Tier 2, UI-designer gated) **or**, per the co-location pattern, beside its component as `<name>.css.ts` (e.g. `overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts`, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/zimmButton.css.ts` — governed by that component's own CODEOWNERS entry instead). Either way it's registered in `theme/components/index.ts`. See [.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md](../.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md) > Co-locating a component's theme file. Note: brand fonts (Futura Round) **are** self-hosted — two faces ship from `overrides/app/static/fonts/` via `theme/fontFace.tsx`, mounted unconditionally, so they are served on every tier. See [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md) > Design System.
- **App shell (Header/Footer):** `overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx`
- **Header:** `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx`
- **Custom components:** `overrides/app/components/custom/`
- **Assets:** `overrides/app/static/`, `overrides/app/assets/svg/`

## Design Source of Truth

Figma file "29 April 2026" is the **current working draft** — not a signed-off final design. Implementations based on it are client-preview builds and may need to be revised when designs are finalised. Do not treat any Figma-derived decision as confirmed without explicit sign-off.

Desktop prototype at zimm-prototype.vercel.app is AI-generated and desktop-only — also not a signed-off final design.

Two rows: top bar (nav + icons) and logo row. Implemented in `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx`, with Chakra theme overrides split across `overrides/app/theme/components/header.ts` and `overrides/app/theme/components/listMenu.ts`.

## Contentful Content Type Management

Content types (schema) are never created manually in the Contentful web app. They are
authored in code as one organization-scoped **Environment Template** and installed into
each environment — Contentful's current recommended mechanism, replacing an earlier
per-environment sync pipeline. This makes schema changes reviewable, repeatable, and
team-safe.

**Key paths:**

- `scripts/contentful/buildTemplate.js` — assembles every content type in the definitions directory into one `EnvironmentTemplate`, get-or-created by name under `CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID`
- `scripts/contentful/setup/installTemplate.mjs` — validates then installs the template's current version into one target environment
- `scripts/contentful/content-types/` — one `.js` file per content type (e.g. `footerConfig.js`), the sole source of truth for its fields (including `localized`/`required`/`validations`)

**To register a new content type:**

1. Add a definition file to `scripts/contentful/content-types/<contentTypeId>.js` (see existing files for shape)
2. Run `npm run sync:contentful`
3. Run `npm run install:contentful -- --target <env>` for each environment in the promotion chain

**To run it:**

```
npm run sync:contentful
npm run install:contentful -- --target dev
```

---
name: code-quality
description: Audit recently changed or specified files for code quality issues — naming, circular imports, TypeScript coverage, test/story existence, and structural debt. Read-only. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR.
---

Audit code quality for the specified scope. Do not modify any files — this is a read-only
diagnostic. Produce a prioritised report with actionable fixes.

---

## Input

The user will provide one of:
- A file path or directory to audit
- No argument — default to files changed on the current branch: `git diff --name-only main`

If no argument is given, run: `git diff --name-only main` and audit those files.
Exclude test files (`*.test.ts`, `*.spec.ts`), stories (`*.stories.tsx`), and any registry files.

---

## Parallel execution

For audits covering more than 5 files, split into four independent checks and run them
as parallel agents simultaneously. Each agent receives only its own checklist — do not
bundle all checks into one agent.

- **Agent A — Naming & structure**
- **Agent B — Import analysis**
- **Agent C — TypeScript coverage**
- **Agent D — Test & story coverage**

For 5 files or fewer, run all checks sequentially in a single pass.

---

## Agent A — Naming & structure

Rules are defined once, split across [.claude/rules/conventions.md](../../rules/conventions.md)
(cross-cutting), [css.md](../../rules/css.md) (Chakra/styling), and
[components.md](../../rules/components.md) (components/hooks/Storybook) — read the relevant
ones first, then apply each rule to the files in scope. Do not re-list the rules here;
that's how the files drift apart.

Walk the file list and audit each file against the relevant section:

# How Zimmermann PWA builds UI — patterns established by PR #56 and PR #59

Repo: `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa`. PR #56 merged as `2dfeb4d`, PR #59 as `8362b3c`.

---

## 1. PR #56 — the token layer

### What changed in `overrides/app/theme/foundation/`

Files touched (merge `2dfeb4d`): `colour.ts` (+83/−70), `typography.ts` (+123/−89), `zimmTokens.ts` (+133/−118), `spacing.ts` (+25/−13), `sizes.ts` (+4/−3), `index.ts` (+2/−2). Plus `theme/globalStyles.ts` (+6/−88) and the new governance doc `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` (+178, new file).

Three structural moves:

1. **`zimmTokens.ts` became fully derived.** Before, every `--zimm-*` value was a hand-retyped literal (`'--zimm-color-grey-900': '#191919'`). After, it imports and references: `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts:6-12` imports `colors`, `fontSizes`, `lineHeights`, `letterSpacings`, `fontWeights`, `spacing`, `borderWidths`, `focusRingOffsets`, `iconSizes`, `actionSizes`, `grid`, `motion`, then maps them (`zimmTokens.ts:16` — `'--zimm-color-grey-black': colors.grey.black`).
2. **`typography.ts` gained a primitive scale layer** it previously lacked — `fontSizes` / `lineHeights` / `letterSpacings` / `fontWeights` (`typography.ts:6-34`), deduplicated out of the 22 named `textStyles` below them (`typography.ts:38-239`).
3. **px → rem for anything that should scale** (WCAG 1.4.4). `spacing.ts:8-22` is entirely rem; px survives only for hairline geometry, and only as named tokens: `borderWidths` (`spacing.ts:26-28`) and `focusRingOffsets` (`spacing.ts:34-37`).

### The literal count

The 237 → 64 figure isn't stated verbatim in the commit or PR body. My independent count corroborates the magnitude: a hex/px/rem/em/rgba regex over code lines only (comments stripped) across `foundation/` gives **256 at `b6841a9`** (PR base) → **75 at `2dfeb4d`** — ~181 removed. Per-file the collapse is concentrated exactly where the derivation happened: `zimmTokens.ts` 105 → 8, `typography.ts` 65 → 13, `colour.ts` 55 → 21. Treat the exact number as approximate; the *architecture* is the checkable thing.

### Resulting token architecture

**Four layers, each a reference to the one below — never a copy.**

| Layer | File | Contains |
|---|---|---|
| Primitive | `foundation/colour.ts:6-37` | `grey`, `ivory`, `coral`, `green`, `orange`, `red`, `opacity` — plain `const`s, the only hex in the system |
| Semantic alias | `foundation/colour.ts:39-113` | `text`, `background`, `border`, `status`, `link`, `icon`, `action` — **read from the primitives** (`text.default: grey[900]`, line 61) |
| Scale primitives | `foundation/spacing.ts`, `typography.ts:6-34`, `sizes.ts`, `motion.ts`, `gridSystem.ts` | rem spacing scale, font sizes/line heights/letter spacings/weights, icon + action sizes |
| CSS-var registry | `foundation/zimmTokens.ts` | the flat `--zimm-*` map, derived from all of the above |

The stated rule is at `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:72` — *"The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy"*: "two values can't disagree if only one of them is ever typed."

**Naming scheme.** `--zimm-<domain>-<path>`:
- `--zimm-color-*` (`--zimm-color-grey-900`, `--zimm-color-text-default`, `--zimm-color-action-primary-bg-hover`)
- `--zimm-scale-*` — named steps (`3xs…7xl`) plus 15 numeric Handover aliases (`--zimm-scale-400`)
- `--zimm-font-size-* / -lineheight-* / -letterspacing-* / -weight-* / -family-*`
- `--zimm-icon-size-*`, `--zimm-size-action-*`, `--zimm-border-width-*`, `--zimm-focus-ring*`, `--zimm-grid-margin-*`, `--zimm-motion-*`

**How tokens get emitted — two separate channels, deliberately:**

- **CSS custom properties** → `overrides/app/theme/zimmTokensGlobal.tsx:16-22` serialises `zimmTokens` into a raw Emotion `<Global>` `:root` block. It is **not** Chakra's `styles.global` — `zimmTokensGlobal.tsx:7-10` records why: Chakra's style processor mangles quoted font-family values, collapsing `"'Futura Round', 'Century Gothic', sans-serif"` to one family. Mounted at `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx:160` (and in `.storybook/preview.tsx`, so app and Storybook cannot drift).
- **Chakra theme scales** → `overrides/app/theme/index.ts:51-64`. Only six foundations are registered: `borderWidths, breakpoints, colors, fonts, space: spacing, textStyles`. `theme/index.ts:31-45` documents which are deliberately **not** registered and why — `fontSizes`, `transition` and `sizes` collide by key name with Chakra defaults used at ~199 base-template call sites (Chakra `sizes.lg` = 32rem vs `iconSizes.lg` = 20px).

### The rule for reaching for a value

`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:12-37` — strict order:

1. `textStyle` prop for anything textual — never a raw `fontSize` (line 14)
2. Raw `var(--zimm-*)` for colour and spacing — **never a bare Chakra token string** like `color="text.default"` even though it resolves correctly (line 16)
3. The component's own theme config — `theme/components/<name>.ts` or a co-located `<name>.css.ts` (line 28)
4. `sx` for a one-off prop-system gap (line 35)
5. Scoped `.scss` only when `sx` genuinely can't express it (line 36)

Line 39: **"Never: a raw hex/px/rem/em literal in a component file."**

### When a raw literal *is* acceptable

Three legitimate cases, all with evidence in-tree:

- **`foundation/` itself** — out of scan scope; a raw value there is the point (`scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs:12-14`).
- **Genuinely context-relative units** — `em` for breakpoints. `theme/components/footerShared.ts:15-17` carries an explicit `audit-allow:` for exactly this: *"raw em is correct and permanent here, not a placeholder awaiting a token."*
- **A value with no token yet, pending designer sign-off** — must be a **named constant with an explanatory comment**, never an inline literal. Canonical examples: `zimmButton.css.ts:202-207` (`BTN_HEIGHT_LG = '50px'`, `BTN_HEIGHT_SM`, `BTN_PADDING_Y`), `footer.css.ts:3-13` (`SPACE_SECTION`, `SIZE_COL_SUB`, `SIZE_COL_MAP`, `COLOUR_HALF_INV`), `zimmNavItem.css.ts:2-11` (`NAV_ITEM_PAD_Y = '4.5px'`).

### `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` — what it actually enforces

| Aspect | Detail |
|---|---|
| Command | `npm run audit:tokens` (`package.json:76`) |
| Scan roots | `overrides/app/components/**` and `overrides/app/theme/components/**` (line 54) |
| Extensions | `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.scss` (line 55) |
| Excluded files | `*.test.ts`, `*.test.tsx`, `*.stories.tsx` (lines 61-62) |
| Excluded path | `theme/foundation/` — not under either root (lines 12-14) |
| Patterns | `HEX_RE = /#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}\b/g` (line 57); `UNIT_RE = /\b\d+(?:\.\d+)?(?:rem|em|px)\b/g` (line 58) |
| Comment handling | `stripComments()` (lines 83-104) removes `//` and `/* */` so a Figma hex quoted in prose isn't flagged. `//` is not treated as a comment when preceded by `:` — otherwise `'https://wa.me/…'` truncates the line |
| Exit code | `1` if any unacknowledged finding (line 167) |
| CI status | **Not wired into CI** (lines 42-43, and `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:231-238`). Advisory only |

**The escape hatch.** `EXCEPTION_MARKER_RE = /provisional|pending|placeholder|audit-allow/i` (line 59). A match is downgraded from failure → *acknowledged exception* (printed, but doesn't affect exit code) when **the contiguous non-blank block of lines ending at the match** contains one of those words (lines 119-122).

Two design details worth encoding in a skill:
- The context window is "up to the nearest blank line or file start", **not a fixed N lines** (lines 29-34). This is because real exception comments in this repo are multi-line shared blocks (`footer.css.ts`'s four constants share one comment) or wrap the marker across a line break.
- There is **no separate allow-list file** — the explanatory comment *is* the allow-list entry (lines 25-27), specifically to avoid a second list that drifts.

### The second, *hard* gate: `recipeGuards.test.ts`

`overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` runs on every `npm run test` and **fails the build**. Five guards (bodies at lines 286-364):

1. `no sizing property uses a bare spacing-scale key` (295) — `width: 'xl'` reads Chakra `sizes.xl` (36rem), not `space.xl`. Shipped a 576px icon and collapsed the footer.

4. `no override-component style uses a bare token key on a registered scale` (331) — **house style**, not a bug: `gap: 'xs'` resolves correctly but must be `var(--zimm-scale-xs)`.
5. `no recipe silently inherits a base SFCC recipe of the same name` (347) — `extendTheme` deep-merges, so a recipe named `Footer` *inherits* SFCC's `Footer` instead of replacing it. `INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu']`; everything else must be namespaced `Zimm*`.

### Focused recipe vs shared style surface

**Focused, co-located recipe** — `footer/footerNavColumn/footerNavColumn.css.ts`:
- Owns one component's own layout. Exports one recipe object (`ZimmFooterNavColumn`) with `parts: ['col','heading','list','listItem']` + `baseStyle`.

- Consumed by name, not by path: `footerNavColumn/index.tsx:7` `const ZIMM_FOOTER_NAV_COLUMN_RECIPE = 'ZimmFooterNavColumn'` → `useMultiStyleConfig(...)` at line 35.
- Comments carry the Figma node ID and the measurement reasoning (`footerNavColumn.css.ts:6-25` — a 15-line justification of the 160px cap, including the 13% fallback-font width delta).
- **CODEOWNERS routes it to the squads only** (`CODEOWNERS:186` — `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` → `@pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b`), last-match-wins deliberately overriding the Tier 2 `overrides/app/components/footer/` rule at `CODEOWNERS:87`.

**Shared style surface** — `theme/components/footerShared.ts`:
- Exports only values needed by **more than one** split-out file: `BP` (breakpoints) and `SIZE_COL_NAV`.
- It stays in `theme/components/` → **Tier 2, UI-designer gated** (`CODEOWNERS:117`).
- It is **not itself a recipe** — it's not in `theme/components/index.ts`'s `components` export.
- It's the one place allowed to import `foundation/` directly, with the reason stated at `footerShared.ts:13-14`: *"Media queries cannot consume var(), so this is the one deliberate exception."*

**The decision rule**, stated at `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:239-244`:

> **Cross-file shared values** (a breakpoint or provisional size needed by more than one split-out file) go in a small shared module that stays in `theme/components/` — e.g. `footerShared.ts`… Don't copy the same literal into two co-located files.

Restated as a checkable test:

| Question | Answer → location |
|---|---|
| Used by exactly one component? | co-located `<name>.css.ts` beside it |
| Needed by ≥2 split-out files of the same feature? | a shared module in `theme/components/` (`footerShared.ts`) |
| Is it a **new raw design value** (authoring a token, not composing one)? | `theme/foundation/` (Tier 1) or a still-gated `theme/components/*.ts` — `overrideStyling.md:212-215` |
| Is it app-wide, static, non-interactive, massively reused? | `theme/globalStyles.ts` `.zimm-*` class (`overrideStyling.md:104-106`) |

Registration is uniform regardless of file location: everything lands in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` (19 recipes, lines 21-41), because *"Chakra resolves a recipe by the string key passed to `useMultiStyleConfig`, not by file path, so co-location is purely an organisational choice with no runtime difference"* (`overrideStyling.md:201-205`).

### Other hard patterns PR #59 established

- **Namespace every new recipe `Zimm*`.** `overrideStyling.md:169-172` and enforced by guard 5. `theme/components/footer.ts` was deliberately named `ZimmFooter`, not `Footer`.
- **Responsive steps are explicit media queries, not Chakra's array shorthand** (`overrideStyling.md:224-236`): ``[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: { gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)' }``. The array form (`['2xs','2xs','xs','xs']`) puts a bare token key at every step and fails guard 4. `footer.css.ts`'s `contentRow` (line 38) and `linksInner` (line 71) are the reference.
- **Multipart vs single-part.** Multipart = plain object with `parts: [...]` + `baseStyle`, consumed via `useMultiStyleConfig` (11 of 13 co-located recipes). Single-part = `defineStyleConfig({baseStyle, variants, defaultProps})`, consumed via `useStyleConfig` — only `zimmButton.css.ts` and `zimmNavItem.css.ts`.
- **Presentational + container split in one file.** `footer/index.tsx` exports `Footer` (named, required `data` prop, fetches nothing, lines 68-133) and `FooterContainer` (default, owns the Contentful fetch, lines 172-217). The JSDoc at lines 158-171 explains why the seam exists at all: base `_app/index.jsx` renders `<Footer />` with no props, so there is no upstream container.
- **Fixtures live in a sibling `index.stories.content.ts`**, typed against the real Contentful type, and only ever feed the presentational export (`footer/index.stories.content.ts:1-9`).
- **Stories carry `play` for security-adjacent behaviour**, not just visuals — `footer/index.stories.tsx:28-40` asserts `target="_blank"` + `rel="noopener noreferrer"` + the WCAG 3.2.5 accessible-name suffix.

## 3. atoms / molecules / organisms — as actually practised

### Current inventory

| Tier | Components |
|---|---|
| **atoms** (11) | zimmButton, zimmIcon, zimmLogo, zimmModal, zimmNavItem, zimmTextInput, zimmProductName, zimmProductPrice, zimmProductDescription, zimmProductModelInfo, zimmProductStyleCode |
| **molecules** (4) | zimmContactIconRow, zimmInputAction, zimmProductContent, zimmProductMeta |
| **organisms** (2) | zimmSubscribeModal, zimmSubscribeSection |

### What actually distinguishes them

The operative distinction is **what a component is allowed to import and own**, not size:

**Atom — imports no other ui-kit component; owns no cross-component state.**
- `zimmNavItem` (`atoms/zimmNavItem/index.tsx`) — one `<a>` or `<button>`. Imports nothing from ui-kits. Its whole visual contract (hover underline, focus ring, `light`/`inverse` variants) is in `zimmNavItem.css.ts`.
- `zimmProductStyleCode` (`atoms/zimmProductStyleCode/index.tsx`) — renders one line, returns nothing when the value is absent. Single prop `value?: string`.
- `zimmModal` (`atoms/zimmModal/index.tsx`) — deliberately owns *no content*: portal + backdrop + accessible dialog panel, caller supplies children. That's what keeps it an atom despite being structurally involved.

**Molecule — composes ≥2 atoms; may own trivial local UI state; owns no business/domain state.**
- `zimmInputAction` (`molecules/zimmInputAction/index.tsx:1-5`) imports `ZimmTextInput` + `ZimmButton` + `ZimmIconType`. It holds one `useState` for a validation string (line 26) — presentation-local only. Notably it has **no `.css.ts`** at all; it borrows its children's recipes and adds a single inline `__css` on the form (line 60).
- `zimmContactIconRow` composes three `ZimmIcon`s into a labelled row; the JSDoc explicitly says *"nothing here is footer-specific"* — reusability is part of the tier claim.
- `zimmProductMeta` = `ZimmProductModelInfo` + `ZimmProductStyleCode` — the whole component is two atoms in design order.

**Organism — composes molecules/atoms **and** reaches outside itself: a custom hook, app-wide context, or another organism.**
- `zimmSubscribeSection` (`organisms/zimmSubscribeSection/index.tsx:1-6`) is the clearest case. It imports `ZimmInputAction` (molecule) + `ZimmSubscribeModal` (organism) **and** `useSubscribeSection` (a hook owning a 4-state machine: idle/success/unavailable/error) **and** `useUiCopy` (app-wide Contentful-backed context). It has its own `index.test.tsx`.
- `zimmSubscribeModal` — composes `ZimmModal` + form fields into a complete, self-contained feature unit with a defined job.

Rough correlate: atoms have 1-3 props; organisms are the tier that gets `index.test.tsx` and a hook.

### Is it documented?

**No — it is purely implied by placement, plus two soft conventions.** I searched every `.md`, `.ts`, `.tsx` outside `node_modules`: there is **no file anywhere that defines atom vs molecule vs organism.** Neither `.claude/rules/components.md`, `.claude/rules/conventions.md`, `.claude/skills/new-component/SKILL.md`, nor `.docs/architecture.md` mentions the words. The only references are incidental (`.claude/rules/testing.md:16` cites an organism's test as an example; `overrideStyling.md:201`, `:249` cite paths).

The two conventions that *do* carry the signal:

1. **JSDoc first word.** Every ui-kit component's docblock opens `Atom — …` / `Molecule — …` (e.g. `atoms/zimmNavItem/index.tsx:28`, `molecules/zimmInputAction/index.tsx:24`, `molecules/zimmProductContent/index.tsx:39`). The two organisms are the inconsistency: neither says "Organism —"; `zimmSubscribeSection/index.tsx:30` says *"Newsletter sign-up organism"* mid-sentence.
2. **`.claude/registry/components.md`** — auto-generated by `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs`, mirrors those JSDoc first lines into a table (lines 85-101). It surfaces the tier but doesn't define it.

**Critically: the folder tier is orthogonal to the Storybook category.** `.claude/rules/components.md:131` defines `Foundation/ Elements/ Layout/ Commerce/ Forms/ Pages/ Contentful/` — a *domain* taxonomy. Atoms land in both `Elements/` (zimmButton, zimmNavItem, zimmModal) and `Commerce/` (zimmProductPrice, zimmProductName); molecules land in `Elements/` (zimmContactIconRow), `Forms/` (zimmInputAction) and `Commerce/` (zimmProductMeta); organisms land in `Forms/`. A skill must not conflate the two.

**Gap worth flagging for the skill:** these are the two rules most likely to be silently violated, because nothing checks them. A workflow skill could mechanically enforce (a) JSDoc starts with `Atom —`/`Molecule —`/`Organism —` matching the parent folder, and (b) an atom's `index.tsx` contains no import from `../../molecules/` or `../../organisms/`.

## 4. Override vs. custom — the decision

### The documented rule (and its staleness)

`.docs/architecture.md:127-130`:

> - **Overriding a base template component:** copy from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path in `overrides/`.
> - **Brand-new components** (no base template equivalent): create them in `overrides/app/components/custom/`.

**`overrides/app/components/custom/` does not exist.** The directory listing is `_app-config, contentful, footer, foundation, header, icons, pageContainer, product-view, ui-kits, uiCopyProvider`. PR #59 established `ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/` as the real home for brand-new components, and `.docs/architecture.md:130` was never updated. `CODEOWNERS:173-176` now describes `ui-kits/` as *"the shared design-system layer consumed by both squads' component overrides"* — i.e. the custom tier, under a different name. **A workflow skill should encode `ui-kits/`, and flag architecture.md:130 as stale.**

### The actual decision procedure

**Does a base file exist at the mirrored path in `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/…`?**

**Yes → override.** Then the **Copy-first rule** is mandatory and blocking (`AGENTS.md` > Rules > Copy-first; `.docs/architecture.md:120-125`):
1. Copy the file to the mirrored path in `overrides/`
2. Convert `.js`/`.jsx` → `.ts`/`.tsx`, replace `PropTypes` with TS types, no `as any` / `@ts-ignore`
3. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
4. Add a temporary `console.log('[overrides] …')` to prove the override is rendering
5. **Stop and present to the user** before any functional change

Filename discipline: an override keeps the base kebab-case name (`product-tile/index.tsx`); Zimmermann-authored is camelCase (`.claude/rules/conventions.md:76-79`).

**No → custom**, under `ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<zimmComponentName>/`.

### Two extra constraints that are actually the sharp edges

**a) If the base component is used internally by SFCC's own components, the default export must stay a faithful port.** `overrideStyling.md:173-186`: check with `grep -r "from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'" node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`. If it's an internal dependency, keep the default export API-compatible and put brand styling behind a named export (`product-tile`'s `CardBaseline` + default) or, preferably now, a theme recipe.

**b) Import an already-overridden component by *relative* path, never the base path.** `overrideStyling.md:150-166`. The `ccExtensibility` resolver only runs in the real webpack build — `.storybook/main.js` aliases straight to `node_modules` and `vitest.config.ts` doesn't touch it. A base-path import ships correctly but **silently renders the unstyled base SFCC component in Storybook and Vitest**. A known unfixed instance is named: `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice` import.

### Evidence from the two PRs

- **PR #59 did both, on the same feature.** `footer/index.tsx` is an *override* (mirrors base `app/components/footer`, keeps kebab-case, default export is what SFCC renders) — while its six new building blocks are *custom* (`ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton`, `zimmIcon`, `zimmLogo`, `zimmNavItem`, `zimmTextInput`, `ui-kits/molecules/zimmInputAction`). The dividing line is exactly "does a base file exist at that path."
- **PR #59 also relocated a recipe across the boundary**: `theme/components/button.ts` (deleted, −119) → `ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/zimmButton.css.ts` (+251). The governance consequence is flagged, unresolved, in `overrideStyling.md:218-226`: the move dropped those provisional constants out of the designer's Tier 2 gate, and the doc says explicitly *"Whether `zimmButton.css.ts` should be re-gated is an open governance question, not a doc fix, and is deliberately left open here."*
- **PR #56's scoping decision** is the other direction: `link.ts` was cut from the PR because *"the component doesn't exist on `develop` yet"* — a theme recipe is not created ahead of the component it styles.

## 5. Contentful integration

There are **two entirely separate paths**, and conflating them is the main failure mode.

### Path A — Studio Experiences (drag-and-drop page builder)

Directory: `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/`. Only files here are processed.

Developer steps (`.claude/skills/contentful-register-component/SKILL.md`, and `scripts/contentful/generateDefinitions.mjs:1-22`):

1. Put the component in `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/<name>.tsx`
2. Add `/** @cf-register */` immediately before the component's `const` declaration
3. Annotate each exposed prop: `/** @cf Display Name */` or `/** @cf Display Name, control */`
4. `npm run generate:contentful` → rewrites `experiences/definitions.ts` (never hand-edited)
5. Verify with `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run generate:contentful:check` (exits 0 if in sync)

Mechanics: ts-morph AST walk. Controls are `shortText | longText | select | toggle | number | media` (`generateDefinitions.mjs:43-51`). Inference: `string→shortText`, `boolean→toggle`, `number→number`, string-literal union→`select`. Auto-skipped: `on*` handlers and `children` (emits `children: true`). Component `id` = kebab-case of the filename; `name` = Title Case. **Untagged non-handler props fail loudly.** The pre-commit hook auto-runs the generator when an `experiences/*.tsx` file is staged (`scripts/hooks/pre-commit:127-164`).

**Current state: empty.** `experiences/definitions.ts` calls `defineComponents([])` — PR #59 deleted `hotspotMarker.tsx`, `hotspotPopup.tsx`, `shoppableImage.tsx` (unused Hardi-era scaffolding). The file's header (lines 3-8) documents the hand-restored empty state because the generator refuses to write output when zero components are found. `overrides/app/components/contentful/index.ts` is now an empty file.

### Path B — content-model-driven components (what PR #59 actually used)

This is the live path. **Four steps:**

**1. Define the content type in code** — `scripts/contentful/content-types/<contentTypeId>.js`, one file per type, sole source of truth for fields including `localized`/`required`/`validations`. Existing: `footerConfig.js`, `footerNavGroup.js`, `link.js`, `region.js`, `image.js`, `uiCopy.js`. Then:
```
npm run sync:contentful                       # builds the org-scoped Environment Template
npm run install:contentful -- --target dev    # per environment in the promotion chain
```
(`.docs/architecture.md:160-196`; `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md` > Contentful Schema Definitions — Tier 2, Integration/SI owned. Field deletion is opt-in via `--delete-deleted-fields`, off by default.)

**2. Mirror the shape in TypeScript** — `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts`. Types present: `RegionEntry` (:64), `LinkEntry` (:86), `FooterNavGroupEntry` (:102), `FooterConfigEntry` (:121), `UiCopyEntry` (:158). `architecture.md:194` states the rule: *"The content type's field IDs must match the TypeScript type in `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts`."*

**3. Register the ID** — `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts`, `CONTENT_TYPE_IDS`: `region, link, footerNavGroup, footerConfig, uiCopy`. This file also owns per-tier environment mapping (`dev/test/sit/staging/uat/master`) and locale→site mapping.

**4. Fetch in a container, render in a presentational component.** `FooterContainer` (`footer/index.tsx:172-217`) uses `useContentfulClient()` → `client.getEntries({content_type: 'footerConfig', include: FOOTER_INCLUDE_DEPTH})` → `pickMostSpecificByRegion` → `scopeToRegion`. The presentational `Footer` takes `data: FooterConfigEntry` as a required prop and fetches nothing.

### Content types involved and their roles

| Type | Role |
|---|---|
| `footerConfig` | Root entry — subscribe copy, `navGroups[]`, `legalLinks[]`, `copyrightOwner`, `phoneHref`/`whatsAppHref`/`emailHref`, `regions[]` |
| `footerNavGroup` | One nav column — heading, `links[]`, `showContactChannels` |
| `link` | `{label, href, regions[]}` — the reusable, region-scopable link |
| `region` | `{siteId, label, locale}` — maps a Contentful entry to an SFCC site |
| `uiCopy` | One entry per UI string: `{title, key (unique, non-localized), value (localized), description}` |

### Three project-specific gotchas a skill should encode

1. **`include` depth is load-bearing and fails hard.** `footer/index.tsx:17-27`: the footer model is exactly three levels (`footerConfig → navGroups → links → regions`). At depth 2 the `regions` array arrives as unresolved link stubs with no `fields`, `region.fields.siteId` throws, `.catch` swallows it, and **the entire footer renders nothing.** Note `useContentful.ts` hardcodes 2 for asset resolution — a different concern, not a house default.

2. **Region scoping is applied in code, not by Contentful.** `overrides/app/utils/resolveByRegion.ts` — `filterByRegion` (inclusive, for arrays where multiple regional entries coexist) vs `pickMostSpecificByRegion` (precedence: fewer `regions` = more specific; unscoped sorts last, `specificity()` returns `Infinity`).

3. **Failure behaviour is deliberately split by content kind.** Structural content fails closed — `FooterContainer` returns `null` rather than substitute placeholder copy (`footer/index.tsx:164-168`). Microcopy fails open — `UiCopyProvider` (`uiCopyProvider/index.tsx:30-33`) states: *"unlike structural content… losing a button label or a status message to a Contentful outage should never blank a control."*

The `uiCopy` pattern is worth calling out as its own reusable primitive: one bulk CDA call per locale for the whole app (`UiCopyProvider`, mounted at `_app-config/index.tsx:161`), assembled into a key→value `Map`, exposed as `t(key, fallback)`. `useUiCopy` degrades to `FALLBACK_ONLY` with no Provider (`hooks/useUiCopy.ts:19-22, :37`), which is why `.claude/rules/components.md:73-88` grants it an explicit exception to the no-data-fetching-in-leaves rule — and why the same paragraph warns that `useIntl` does **not** share that property (it throws, and its Provider sits in base SFCC `_app`, a strictly narrower subtree than `_app-config`).
